ledger.claim: The record cannot establish that the rider was anywhere other than inside Terminal 3. The rider leg of the trace holds 88 fixes and every one of them reports 45 m to 80 m horizontal accuracy, so every one falls outside the 25 m accuracy filter that POL-NS-02 applies to driver fixes and that POL-NS-04(c) applies symmetrically to rider fixes; rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0. The 2,039 m minimum and 2,101 m mean distance those raw fixes report from the pickup pin are therefore inadmissible readings rather than evidence that the rider was away: under POL-NS-04(c) rider fixes below the accuracy filter 'count as evidence of neither presence nor absence', and a rider track whose every fix is filtered out is undecidable and expressly neutral, not adverse. I accept that POL-NS-04 does not otherwise apply here, because limb (a) requires a coordinating message from the rider and the chat log contains none; but the neutrality rule its limb (c) states is what governs this rider track, and on that rule the rider's account that he was in the terminal is neither contradicted nor confirmed by the trace.

Nothing on this record shows the rider was ever reached. The chat log holds three messages and no more — the system arrival notice at 23:13:11, MSG-00202-002 at 23:14:02 and MSG-00202-003 at 23:19:30 — and all three, the platform's own notice included, carry read_at null; the trip record's in_app_calls is empty, so the driver never used the voice channel that POL-NS-04(b) treats as the alternative to a chat reply. I disclose that the chat log is impaired: issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE, weight 0.85, and I rely on it only for what it establishes despite that discount — that the driver's two 'still waiting' texts and the platform's arrival notification were never acknowledged by anyone, and that he cancelled roughly ten minutes after arriving without trying any channel other than unread in-app text. ledger.claim: If the case is to turn on whether this rider should bear the fee at all, that question is not settled by the record and the answer the policy gives is escalation rather than collection. Rider presence is the only fact that speaks to the rider's side of the no-show test, and the only artifact that touches it is the trace, whose rider leg is filtered out in its entirety; POL-NS-04(c) says in terms that this leaves the artifact impaired for the purposes of POL-NS-08(b), and where the sole evidence for a fact is impaired under limb (b) the matter escalates under POL-NS-09 instead of being resolved against the party it disfavours. I again disclose that the chat artifact I cite to show the rider was never reached is impaired (UNREAD_MESSAGE, weight 0.85, per POL-GEN-02(1)). Escalation is terminal and the disputed SGD 6.00 is held rather than collected or refunded while the reviewer settles the open question: whether a rider who was inside Terminal 3, whose arrival notice was never read and whom the driver never telephoned, should be charged a no-show fee on a trace that cannot place him at all.

I do not press the two arithmetic routes that are closed to the rider, and I do not ask the judge to stretch them. The derived dwell is a single continuous qualifying run of 620 seconds — 63 fixes from 23:12:45 to 23:23:05 inside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius — against the 480 second AIRPORT minimum, a surplus of 140 seconds (shortfall_sec -140.0), so no waiting-period shortfall argument under POL-NS-06 is available; and the same derived facts put the driver in-radius and holding position 25 seconds before he tapped 'arrived' at 23:13:10, so no false-arrival argument under POL-NS-05 is available either. The rider's case rests on the points above, not on those.

Limb (a) of the chargeable-no-show test is met on the face of the record: the trip record for TRP-00202 carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-07-24T23:13:10+08:00, and the trip is recorded as cancelled by the driver, not abandoned before arrival.

Limb (b) is met: the driver's GPS trace has him inside the AIRPORT arrival radius of 150 m at and before the arrival event — the qualifying in-geofence run opens at 23:12:45, a full 25 seconds before the 23:13:10 arrival marker, and the trace's closest approach to the pin is 22.4 m, far inside the 150 m radius the fee schedule sets for the Changi kerbside.

Limb (c) is met with room to spare: the driver held position inside the geofence in a single unbroken qualifying run of 63 GPS fixes lasting 620 seconds, from 23:12:45 to 23:23:05. That clears the 480-second AIRPORT minimum by 140 seconds; the shortfall field reads -140.0, i.e. a surplus, and limb (c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying fix and not from the arrival tap, which is exactly how this run is computed.

Limb (d) is met: the trip record shows no boarding event and records the trip terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW at 23:23:20 — fifteen seconds AFTER the required 480-second dwell elapsed at 23:23:05, so the cancellation falls at or after the moment the dwell was complete as limb (d) requires. The reason code is one of the three limb (d) recognises, and this is not a DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE case that would divert the matter to POL-NS-03.

POL-NS-05 does not defeat the fee, because the arrival marker is not false. At 23:13:10 the driver was already stationary inside the 150 m radius — the dwell had opened 25 seconds earlier — so he was neither more than 300 m from the pin nor travelling at or above the 15 km/h motion threshold at the moment the marker was set. The clause's own limb (iii) confirms a marker set by a driver who then genuinely waits the full period does not void an otherwise good fee.

Limb (a) requires a rider chat message that locates or coordinates, and the chat log contains only the system 'driver has arrived' notice and two driver messages — there is no rider message at all, so limb (a) fails before limb (b) or (c) is reached. Limb (c) would in any event be undecidable rather than satisfied: every one of the rider's 88 fixes reports 45 m to 80 m horizontal accuracy and is filtered out, leaving rider_qualifying_fix_count at 0, which POL-NS-04 expressly makes neutral rather than adverse.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: the SGD 6.00 no-show fee is not refunded, and the reason is the policy's four-part test in POL-NS-01, which this record satisfies on all four limbs. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 23:13:10. (b) The GPS trace (weight 1.0, 116 fixes, zero gaps, 100% coverage) puts the driver inside the 150 m Changi Terminal 3 arrival radius from 23:12:45 — 25 seconds before the 'arrived' tap — with a closest approach of 22.4 m. (c) He held station there in a single unbroken qualifying run of 63 fixes lasting 620 seconds, against the 480-second AIRPORT minimum, a surplus of 140 seconds. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 23:23:20 as RIDER_NO_SHOW, 15 seconds after the required dwell elapsed, with no boarding event. Your two arithmetic arguments are correct and I accept them: POL-NS-05 does not help you (the marker was not false — the driver was already stationary in-radius when he tapped it) and POL-NS-06 does not help you (there is no dwell shortfall to refund). Your point that the rider leg of the trace is undecidable is also correct: all 88 rider fixes report 45–80 m accuracy and are filtered out, so the trace neither places you in the terminal nor proves you away from it, and I treat it as neutral rather than adverse. But rider presence is not what decides this fee: POL-NS-01 nowhere requires the rider to have been present, and the clause that would have used your presence, POL-NS-04, does not apply because its limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating message from you in the chat log, and the log contains no rider message at all. For the same reason I reject the argument that the case must escalate on the rider track: POL-NS-09(e) escalates only where the deciding fact is carried solely by an artifact impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d), and here the deciding facts — arrival, dwell and termination — are carried by the GPS trace and the trip record at full weight. I accept that neither you nor the platform's arrival notice read the driver's two texts (all read_at null, and trip_record.in_app_calls empty), which is why an in-app message was not a reasonable way to reach you; but an unread message does not defeat a fee the driver otherwise earned, and the chat impairment goes to weight, not to the outcome. To the driver: your POL-NS-01 showing is accepted in full, and because no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, POL-NS-07 gives you compensation of 80 percent of the SGD 6.00 fee — SGD 4.80 — with the rider's charge standing unchanged. The anti-farming check does not bite, and both limbs are required: no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below 4) and 1/168 is 0.006 (below 0.08). Two artifacts are impaired at schema level and I name them as POL-GEN-02(3) requires: the chat log EV-CHAT-00202 at weight 0.85 (UNREAD_MESSAGE) and the driver profile EV-DPROF-00202 at weight 0.9 (SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH); neither carries the deciding fact, both are down-weighted in confidence only, and the EUR finding survives because the arrival, dwell and termination rest on the GPS trace and trip record at weight 1.0. The confidence is set by the lowest-weighted artifact that carries part of the decision, the driver profile at 0.9, which is above the 0.70 floor. Some of the driver's specific submissions were discarded by the referee for failing to disclose the impairment of artifacts they cited; that discarding does not change this outcome, which follows from the policy and the record. No clause produces a referral here: the false-arrival referral in POL-NS-05(ii) is not reached (qualifying in-geofence fixes exist), and no driver-conduct or billing-integrity referral fires.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
